explanation: Starting after the designated opener, count nested openers. A closer at nesting depth zero is its matching closer.
correctness: Depth counts unmatched nested openers strictly after the designated opener. A closer with depth>0 belongs to a nested pair and reduces depth. A closer encountered at depth zero closes the designated opener, so returning immediately finds exactly its match.
walkthrough: In x(ab(cd)e)y with opening index 1, start scanning index 2 with nested depth 0. The opener at index 4 raises depth to 1; the closer at index 7 lowers it to 0. The closer at index 9 arrives while depth is zero, so return 9.
edgeCases: An adjacent () returns the next index; nested pairs must close before the designated pair. The bank guarantees that a matching closer exists.
timeComplexity: O(n) worst-case time: scan forward from the supplied opener until its match, visiting each intervening character once.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: an integer depth replaces a stack because only one bracket type matters.
